exclude.reason: Dated per-lane gate evidence: run transcripts, machine paths and the defects of a past lane. It is history for the repository that built the package, not content for an installed one - publishing it would ship internal paths and stale proof. Retained in the repository, excluded from the publish artifact.

The Phase-0 census of the fleet tree (counts, derivation commands, migration inventory). Provenance for the migration; it describes a tree an installer does not have, so it is excluded from the publish artifact.

pathAllowlist.reason: Byte-identical vendored runbook (archived row). The absolute paths are this box's machine facts (the XDG data dir, the provider log) that the prose explains; the canonical owner owns the text and the package must not fork it.
Help-block example of a file-source target (a generic illustration, not a resolution path). The tool itself resolves the lock at the profile state root.
Documented fallback for the Paseo CLI install location on Windows; every caller can override it, and a missing file is handled as absent.
The -PaseoExe parameter default is the Paseo install location; it is a parameter, so a deployment overrides it and the package does not depend on that path.
Deprecated shim with the same -PaseoExe default as Repair-Paseo.ps1.
Help-block example showing the -Root argument; the tool takes the repository root as a parameter.
Documentation of the live XDG data directory on this box; the script resolves XDG_DATA_HOME at run time and the literal appears only in comments.
Example commands for the Paseo CLI at its install location; a deployment substitutes its own path.
The watch runbook names this box's provider log as an example of where to spot-check a quota error; the member reads the profile's provider_log adapter, not this string.
Fixture argv paths (quoted paths containing spaces) that pin the helper command-line quoting rule; they are inputs to a unit test, never resolved.
Worked examples in help and comments naming a fleet checkout; the worker takes its repo root from arguments and resolves nothing from that string.
Help-block and comment examples of a repo path, plus the record of a fixed defect where a repo path was joined onto the record root. The registry takes -Repo/-RepoPath as arguments.
Help-block examples of -RepoPath; the landing test requires the repo path as an argument and never defaults to one.
WELL_KNOWN_WIN is a last-resort location for the Paseo CLI after the environment and PATH checks; it is a documented machine default with an override.
